title: Cameras
description: The cameras of a research project. What a visit does to a camera (put it up, take it away, find it stolen) is what changes its status.
x-rules: label is unique in the research project, whatever its case; so is camera_id when it has one.
An archived camera says why (archive_reason): lost, stolen, broken or other. It never goes back to planned, ready or active.
status: ready (available, not in the field), active (it is up at a location); the visits change it, not a person.
A camera can be up at one location at a time.

items.description:
One of the camera traps — its label (what it is called), optionally its id (the serial number) and its model, as Camtrap DP names
them, and the day it was put into production.

label.description: What the camera is called — the name it goes by in the field.

camera_id.description: The camera's id — its serial number. (cameraID)

camera_model.description: Manufacturer and model, written as manufacturer-model. (cameraModel)

connectivity.description: The mobile network the camera sends its photos through: none when it does not.

power_source.description: What it runs on: cells (AA, AAA… the ones that are changed) or a battery.

battery_removable.description: Whether the battery can be taken out of the camera: only said of a battery, as cells are always taken out to be changed.

in_service.description: The day it was put into production.

status.description: Planned: only in Settings, not in the app. Ready: available, not in the field yet. Active: in use. Archived: out of use for good (see archive_reason).

archive_reason.description: Why it was archived; other when it is none of the others (the status note says it).

status_date.description: The day it stopped being active.

id.description: Its internal id — a UUID the app generates when it is kept, that never changes and is never typed: what the records that refer to it point to.

created_at.description: When it was kept here (ISO 8601, UTC, with a Z): written by the app, never typed.

updated_at.description: When it was last changed (ISO 8601, UTC, with a Z): written by the app, never typed.

deleted_at.description: When it was removed (ISO 8601, UTC, with a Z), if it was: it is no longer listed, but it is kept — nothing is deleted.
